record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Singularities of Mappings
record.context_brief: Mond conjecture for image Milnor number
record.original_question: Let f: (C^n,S) -> (C^(n+1),0) be a complex analytic map-germ of finite A_e-codimension. Here A_e-codimension is the complex vector-space dimension of theta(f)/(t f(theta_{C^n,S}) + omega f(theta_{C^(n+1),0})), and the image Milnor number mu_I(f) is the number of n-spheres in the wedge homotopy type of the image of a stable perturbation of f. For every n such that (n,n+1) lies in Mather's nice dimensions, must mu_I(f) be at least A_e-codim(f), with equality exactly when f is quasihomogeneous?

evidence.quote: The number of n-spheres in the wedge is called the image Milnor number of f, and denoted by muI.
(1.5) muI >= Ae - codim(f), with equality if and only if f is quasihomogeneous.
Conjecture 1.5. (1.5) holds for all values of n for which (n, n+ 1) are in Mather's nice dimensions

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,S)\to(\mathbb{C}^{n+1},0)$ be a complex analytic multi-germ of finite $\mathcal{A}_e$-codimension, where $S\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ is a finite set. Denote by $\theta_{\mathbb{C}^n,S}$ and $\theta_{\mathbb{C}^{n+1},0}$ the modules of germs of vector fields, and let $\theta(f)$ be the module of germs of vector fields along $f$. Define
$$\mathcal{A}_e\text{-codim}(f)=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\frac{\theta(f)}{tf(\theta_{\mathbb{C}^n,S})+\omega f(\theta_{\mathbb{C}^{n+1},0})},$$
where $tf(\xi)=df\circ\xi$ and $\omega f(\eta)=\eta\circ f$. Assume $(n,n+1)$ lies in Mather's nice dimensions, so that $f$ admits a stable perturbation $f_t$. The image of $f_t$ has the homotopy type of a wedge of $n$-spheres; let $\mu_I(f)$, the image Milnor number, denote the number of spheres in this wedge.

Prove or disprove: for every such $n$ and every $f$ of finite $\mathcal{A}_e$-codimension,
$$\mu_I(f)\ge \mathcal{A}_e\text{-codim}(f),$$
with equality if and only if $f$ is quasihomogeneous (i.e., $\mathcal{A}$-equivalent to a germ whose components are weighted homogeneous polynomials with positive weights for a common choice of weights on source and target).
artifact.status_search_result: The Mond conjecture is known to hold for $n=1$ (curves to surfaces, de Jong–van Straten / Mond) and for $n=2$ (surfaces in 3-space, Mond), and has been established in special situations (e.g. for wave fronts, for germs arising from certain augmentations/concatenations, and a weak version characterizing stability via $\mu_I=0$). The full conjecture for all $n$ with $(n,n+1)$ in Mather's nice dimensions remains open.

status_evidence.title: A weak version of Mond's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: A weak version: f is stable iff mu_I(f)=0, under nice dimensions hypothesis; the full Mond conjecture remains open in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Only a weak form is proved in general; full conjecture open for n>2.

status_evidence.title: A Proof of the Mond Conjecture for Wave Fronts
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the Mond conjecture in the frontal/wave-front setting.
status_evidence.claim: Special case proved; the general conjecture is not.

status_evidence.title: Mond's conjecture for maps between curves
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the conjecture in the case of maps between curves (n=1).
